## Sep 25 Results: A Near-Perfect Day for the Models

When your predictive framework goes 15-2 with an 88.2% accuracy rate, you're not just getting lucky—you're capturing real signal in the noise. Yesterday's performance represents exactly the kind of consistency we build these models to achieve. Only one miss in seventeen picks suggests our regression coefficients are properly weighted and our contextual adjustments are working as intended.

## Breaking Down the Statistical Performance

Our model averaged 58.6% confidence across all picks, which is exactly where you want to be—high enough to indicate real edge, but not so high that you're overfitting. The single miss came on Braves @ Marlins (61% confidence on Atlanta), which represents a perfectly acceptable outcome given the probabilistic nature of baseball. Even at 61% confidence, we expect to be wrong nearly 4 times out of 10.

## The Doubleheader Edge

Particularly noteworthy was our 4-0 performance across the two doubleheaders (Cubs-Sox and Orioles-Yankees). Doubleheaders present unique analytical challenges—bullpen depletion, lineup adjustments, starter quality variance. Our model's ability to correctly calibrate these factors speaks to the depth of our contextual variables. The Sox sweep and the split-predictions on the Yankees doubleheader both hit, demonstrating we're not just blindly picking favorites.

## Sep 26 Preview: Nationals as the Top Statistical Play

Looking ahead to tomorrow's slate, our highest-confidence play comes from the same venue that delivered yesterday: Nationals Park. The Mets-Nationals rematch features a fascinating pitcher matchup that our models heavily favor Washington.

## The Analytical Case for Washington

At 62% confidence, this represents our strongest conviction play for Sep 26. While I don't have full seasonal statistics on Jonah Tong or Connelly Early loaded into this preview, the model's 62% confidence suggests a meaningful talent/matchup differential. Our regression framework accounts for pitcher quality, recent performance trends, bullpen availability, and home field advantage—all of which are apparently tilting toward the Nationals.

The fact that we correctly called this same venue yesterday (Nationals 61%, which hit) doesn't influence tomorrow's prediction—each game is evaluated independently—but it does suggest our park factor adjustments and understanding of Nationals Park are well-calibrated.

## Expected Value and Bankroll Management

From an EV perspective, a 62% confidence pick offers solid value, particularly if you can find a line that doesn't fully reflect that probability. As always, proper bankroll management suggests limiting exposure to 1-2% of your total bankroll per pick, regardless of confidence level. Even our best picks fail 38% of the time at this confidence interval.

Check back tomorrow as we track whether the Nationals can deliver on this projection and analyze the full Sep 26 slate results.
